_what: fusion's compliance-guard configuration for THIS project. The guard hooks read it from the project root, on every guarded tool call, and merge it over the plugin's own hooks/config.json and then over fusion's built-in defaults. Keys the parser does not recognise are carried through untouched and never reported, which is why these underscore-prefixed notes can live in the file itself.
_inherits: As seeded, this file declares nothing — and a file that declares nothing inherits everything. The effective protected-path list is the plugin's own hooks/config.json list, plus this file itself (see _protectsItself), and it is deliberately NOT restated here: a copy would go stale, and a stale copy of a security-relevant list is worse than a pointer to the live one. Read the plugin's hooks/config.json to see what is protected. A path added to that default later protects this project too, without this file being touched.
_override: To change something, add the key you want to change, in the same shape the plugin's hooks/config.json uses for it. The merge is per LEAF, not per object: a key you declare is taken exactly as you wrote it, and a key you leave out — even inside an object you did declare — inherits the plugin's value first and falls back to fusion's built-in default only when neither file speaks. So {"guard":{"defaultSensitivity":"high"}} raises the sensitivity and keeps every protected path the plugin ships. Narrowing works because a declared value wins outright: "protectedPaths": [] is the empty list, on purpose, not an inheritance. Know that fusion's built-in default for the protected list is ALSO the empty list — only the plugin's file stands between an omitted list and no protection at all. A declared protected entry carries one further consequence: it outranks the FUSION_ALLOW_RULES_WRITE session flag, so a path you protect here stays protected against that flag, and declaring rules/** yourself withdraws the flag from your whole rule directory. A value with the wrong type is dropped and named in a guard advisory, then inherits as if you had omitted it; a file that is not valid JSON is dropped and reported the same way, never ignored in silence.
_turnBudget: Not everything this file configures is the guard. "orchestrator": {"maxTurns": N} is the number of Turns the orchestrator's Phase-2 loop may run before its Max-Turns circuit breaker exits the loop and reports what is left. It merges by the same per-leaf rule as everything above, and it is read once per session by bin/fusion-turn-budget at the orchestrator's Setup — no hook reads it. fusion's own budget is defined in exactly one place, the DEFAULTS in the plugin's hooks/lib/config.ts, and is deliberately not restated in the plugin's hooks/config.json or in any agent prompt, so this file is the only place a project changes it. A value that is not a whole number of 1 or more — 0, a negative, a decimal, a string — is dropped and named in an advisory, then inherits as if it were absent; there is no upper bound, because a project that wants 60 Turns has said so in a git-tracked file.
_guardEnabled: guard.enabled is the one key this file may not set. The guard's on/off switch is read from the plugin layer and fusion's defaults only — a project does not switch off the guard that governs it. A declared value, true or false, is ignored, and the loader reports the ignored key in a guard advisory naming it, on every guarded call until the line is removed, so the key is never silently inert.
_gitTracked: This file belongs in version control, and that is the point of it living at the project root. It decides what the guard protects, so every change to it has to appear in a diff and pass through the same review as the rest of the project. The diff is also what bounds the one gap in _protectsItself below: before this file exists, nothing stops an agent from creating one.
_protectsItself: Once this file exists on disk the guard protects it, whatever this file itself says — an agent cannot unprotect the configuration that governs it. The protection holds when this file declares an empty list, when it lists itself, when it no longer parses, and when guard.enabled: false is written into it; FUSION_ALLOW_RULES_WRITE does not reach it either. Editing, moving or deleting it does not stick: the guard fingerprints this file before every tool call and again afterwards, and when the two differ it writes back the content the file held before the call and halts. That measurement covers the write tools and the shell alike, whatever route the change took, and it names the file the loader actually read, so it holds from a subdirectory working directory too. Creating it is allowed — that is how setup seeds it, so the protection starts only when the file exists, which is the gap _gitTracked bounds. Change it yourself, in your own editor or terminal, where the guard never looks.
_inFusionsOwnSourceTree: In the fusion plugin's own repository the protected-path half of this file has no effect, because the write guard stands down there so that fusion can be developed on itself — and the self-protection above stands down with it. The file is still read there, and a broken one is still reported. guard.enabled cannot be set from this file, anywhere.
